question: Can the existing Candidate C host restore wrapper block a stale-episode restart and provide distinct process-exit, CAS-refusal, broker redelivery/drain, and credential-reuse evidence on the current Docker Desktop target without a new controller or service?

scope.allowed_environment: Read-only preflight and, only if every start-control prerequisite exists, one disposable Compose project on the inventoried local Docker Desktop target with pinned images and synthetic data.
scope.application_consumer: Must remain disabled; no application consumer or application data is used.
scope.prototype_authorization: One bounded Candidate C experiment only. Use the existing versioned wrapper. Minimal disposable experiment code is allowed, but no new controller, service, daemon, privilege proxy, VM, or infrastructure. If no stale-episode start block exists, stop before runtime and report BLOCKED.
scope.controller_boundary: Identify the wrapper identity and Docker/process-manager privileges. Docker daemon access by another host user is a bypass unless separately prevented; do not claim controller exclusivity without evidence.
scope.production_changes: None; no consumer enablement, accepted-spec change, Harness change, FileVault action, purchase, push, PR, or merge.
scope.deliverable: One registration, a bounded preflight/run report, and separate findings for process exit, stale-episode restart denial, broker drain/redelivery, database CAS refusal, and old-credential reuse. No aggregate PASS or qualification claim.

fixed_checks: Before starting any container, identify the exact current wrapper command, normal launch paths, controller identity/permissions, and the stale-episode refusal. restart: no is not a start authorization guard.
If the wrapper or start-block mechanism is absent, or the test needs a new privileged controller/service, stop before runtime, record BLOCKED, and recommend deferring S30-06.
If preflight permits runtime, use one isolated disposable Compose project, unique run identifiers, bounded subprocess timeouts, and cleanup only resources created by this run.
Report process termination and stale-episode start refusal separately. Capture exact container identity, state/PID, restart policy/count, daemon events, and the refusal response.

In a separate CAS scenario, hold a synthetic handler before its protected write; advance the generation; then permit its write attempt and record whether the CAS rejects it. Do not use process termination as CAS evidence.

In a separate broker scenario, terminate the container with a synthetic delivery unacknowledged; inspect connections, channels, consumers, unacknowledged count, and redelivery after a bounded settle interval.

Define credential interpretation before runtime: if old credentials authenticate outside the stopped container, access revocation is UNSATISFIED. Do not relax the requirement after observing the result.
Record every check independently. Process exit alone is not drain; no result qualifies REF-Q, PROD-Q, or S30-06.
decision_rule: Proceed only if existing wrapper/start-control proof exists and the run needs no new privileged service. Otherwise report BLOCKED before runtime and recommend deferring S30-06. Any stale-credential reconnect means the access-revocation requirement remains unsatisfied pending a separate scope decision.
